1154 Messages and Speeches EXECUTIVE ORDERS. Wuirt House, January 4, 1905. Mrs. Evelyn M. Ford may be reinstated to the position of clerk in the office of the Secretary of War without regard to the provisions of Rule IX limiting the period of eligibility to one year from the date of separation. THEODORE ROOSEVELT. Wunrre House, January 9, 1905. Mrs. Elizabeth C. Peters may be reinstated to the position of sewer in the Government Printing Office without regard to the provision of Rule IX limiting the period of eligibility for reinstatements to one year from the date of separation. THEODORE ROOSEVELT. Wurre House, January 27, 1905. The appointment of Mr. E. W. Libbey as telegraph and telephone operator, at $1,000 per annum, in the Department of Commerce and Labor, on July 13, 1903, is approved, and he may be continued in the service without examination under the Civil-Service rules. THEODORE ROOSEVELT. Warre House, June 29, 1905. Mrs. Edna K. Hoyt, who is temporarily employed as clerk in the De- partment of State, may be permanently appointed, without examination under the civil-service rules, with a salary at the rate of $1,200 per annum. (Nort) Done at the request of Secretary Hay, who says she is now the best clerk of her class that he has. THEODORE ROOSEVELT. Wuitsr Hous, July 25, 1905. Mrs. McLanaham, after twelve years’ service, was separated from the position of sewer in the Government Printing Office prior to her mar- riage in 1894. In June, 1903, she was left a widow with three children to support. In view of her unfortunate circumstances and previous efficient service attested by the Public Printer, the Commission recom- mended to the President a special order waiving the rule requiring reinstatement within one year, which was approved by the President July 25, 1903. THEODORE ROOSEVELT.

Signed by President Theodore Roosevelt Thursday, November 28, 1907

General Order No. 57, Navy Dept., December 9, 1907

628912Executive Order 716 — Adjusting Rules for Extra Pay for Navy Gun Pointers1907President of the United States

The White House,

November 28, 1907.

The extra pay allowed gun pointers in accordance with the Executive order of July 25, 1903, shall be allowed a gun pointer regularly detailed as a gun pointer at a gun of the class at which he qualified only as long as he remains qualified: Provided, This order shall be construed as affecting only gun pointers who qualify subsequent to the date of this order.

Theodore Roosevelt.
